predecessors.name: Kingdom of Bosnia
predecessors.text: Hum, which Stjepan Vukcic had held as Duke of Humska zemlja since 1435 and which he now ruled as 'Herceg'

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Herzegovina, the Sanjak of Herzegovina formed in 1470 (S3), and the last fortress Novi, which fell in 1481/82

ledger.x: 1448: Stjepan Vukcic styles himself 'Herceg' and founds the Duchy of Saint Sava.
1463: Mahmud Pasha besieges Blagaj and Stjepan cedes his lands north of it.
1465: the Ottomans take most of the eastern part of the duchy.
1466: Stjepan dies on 22 May (testament dictated at Novi on 21 May) and Blagaj falls; the sons rule from Novi.
1467: most of the remaining duchy is occupied by the Sanjak of Bosnia's governor.
1481: the Ottomans invade and besiege Novi.
1482: the Duchy of Saint Sava ends with the fall of Novi.

wars.name: Duchy of Saint Sava-Ragusan war over Konavle
wars.outcome: Stjepan laid siege to Dubrovnik; peace was concluded in 1454 and Ragusa kept Konavle.

wars.name: War of Herceg Stjepan and his son Vladislav
wars.outcome: 'On March 29, 1452, Vladislav openly declared his hostility against his father'; a treaty followed at Pisce on the Piva between 1 and 5 June (1453 by context); no land changed hands.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Herzegovina
wars.outcome: Mahmud Pasha besieged Blagaj in 1463; the east fell in 1465; by 1467 much was occupied; Vlatko made peace with the sultan in 1470; the last fortress, Novi, fell in December 1481 (S1) or 1482 (S5).

certainty.note: No treaty line is on the pages; the borders are the extent of the lords' holdings and shrink year by year under Ottoman conquest.
